figures.after: Everyone else gets the empty box.
figures.alt: The money followed the people. Google paid a reported $2.7 billion in August 2024 to license Character.AI's technology and hired its founders. Disney has offered jobs to 66 staff at about $60 million a year for three years and made a $20 million opening bid for the technology. Character.AI, in Chapter 11 since 12 October 2026, keeps the app, its users' data and the lawsuits.

Two years, two buyers, one shell. August 2024: Google reportedly pays $2.7 billion to license Character.AI's technology and hires its founders. December 2025: Disney agrees to put $1 billion into OpenAI and let more than 200 characters into Sora. March 2026: OpenAI says it will shut the Sora app, and the Disney deal goes with it. September 2026: Disney hires Character.AI's chief executive as its first chief technology officer. 12 October 2026: Character.AI files for bankruptcy in Delaware. Now: Disney offers jobs to 66 staff and makes a $20 million opening bid for the technology.

figures.after: moving from renting AI to owning it.
figures.alt: The big media companies are moving from renting AI to owning it. Bought: Disney, bidding for Character.AI's team and technology; Netflix, InterPositive, reported at $587 million; Warner Music, Sureel AI in June; WildBrain, Personality AI in August. Not yet: Skydance, which now owns Paramount and Warner Bros; Universal Music; NBCUniversal. Our call, 75% sure: by 1 March 2027 all three will each have announced buying an AI company or its team.
